settings.heading: The rooms of the house
settings.text: We begin with proportion: header, collection, and the quiet of an empty cart. The storefront should feel like a well-lit atelier — nothing competing with the cloth.

settings.heading: Pattern before colour
settings.text: The first toile is always in calico. Online, that discipline becomes information architecture: About, Story, Building of, Journal — rooms that exist before merchandise shouts.

settings.heading: Cloth and token
settings.text: Colour on the site is inherited from Horizon’s tokens so the house can change cloth without rewriting the rooms. Placeholder copy lives here until the atelier replaces it with the season’s true notes.

settings.heading: Light on the worktable
settings.text: Photography will arrive last. Until then, type and space carry the fitting. We would rather show an honest empty wall than a borrowed set.

settings.heading: Opening the door
settings.text: When the first edition is ready, this journal will record the making — not the marketing. Add entries in the theme editor; keep the voice of the house.

settings.heading: Building of
settings.lede: A making-of journal for the house: how a collection is cut, how the rooms of the storefront are composed, and what we refuse along the way. These notes are living copy — replace them as the atelier advances.
